related_questions.question: Who pays the 3.8% Medicare surtax?
related_questions.snippet: A Medicare surtax of 3.8% is charged on the lesser of (1) net investment income or (2) the excess of modified adjusted gross income over a set threshold amount. The threshold is $250,000 for joint filers, $125,000 for married filing separately, and $200,000 for all other filers.

related_questions.question: Why am I being charged additional Medicare tax?
related_questions.snippet: Income up to a threshold amount is subject to the “regular” Medicare tax. Under the Affordable Care Act, taxpayers who earn above a set income level (depending on filing status) pay 0.9% more into Medicare on top of the regular contribution. This extra tax is called the Additional Medicare Tax.
